key_insight: The paper argues that theory of mind in AI should be triggered only when causal conditions make mentalizing warranted, rather than treated as an always-on capability.
engineering_relevance: It offers a resource-rational decision framework for when an AI system should spend compute on social inference, improving efficiency, trust, and robustness in human-machine interaction.
method: Builds a structural causal model (DAG) for ToM in conflict.
Defines four exogenous conditions, five mediators, and a ToM engagement node.
Identifies three causal pathways: tractability, reasoning-depth, and enabling-cause.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation validation, proposes empirical human-machine teaming studies, and frames epistemic accuracy as the main outcome metric.
watch_item: Conflict-optimized mentalizing may raise ethical and deployment concerns if the model is used to infer or manipulate human mental states inappropriately.
paper_title: A Causal Model of Theory of Mind in Conflict for Artificial Intelligence
